title: Two grocers choose their opening hours: dominant strategies, Nash equilibrium and a fee
scenario: Alder Market and Bexley Foods (invented) are the only grocery stores in a town. Each chooses, at the same time and without talking to the other, whether to keep Late hours or Regular hours. The matrix shows each store's weekly profit in hundreds of dollars; in each cell Alder Market's payoff is listed first. Both stores know the matrix.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Identify each store's dominant strategy, if it has one, and every Nash equilibrium.

rubric.point: Alder Market has no dominant strategy, and Bexley Foods' dominant strategy is Late hours.
The only Nash equilibrium is (Alder Regular hours, Bexley Late hours).

parts.sample: Alder Market has no dominant strategy. Bexley Foods' dominant strategy is Late hours (30 > 20 if Alder keeps late hours, 55 > 45 if Alder keeps regular hours). The only Nash equilibrium is Alder Regular hours, Bexley Late hours, with payoffs of 35 and 55.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain, using the numbers in the matrix, why Alder Market does not have a dominant strategy.

rubric.point: Gives both comparisons for Alder: if Bexley chooses Late, Regular is better (35 > 25); if Bexley chooses Regular, Late is better (60 > 48).

parts.sample: If Bexley keeps late hours, Alder earns 25 from Late and 35 from Regular, so Regular is better. If Bexley keeps regular hours, Alder earns 60 from Late and 48 from Regular, so Late is better. Alder's best choice depends on Bexley's, so it has no dominant strategy.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The town starts charging Bexley Foods a fee of 15 (hundred dollars) a week whenever it keeps Late hours. Identify every Nash equilibrium after the fee.

rubric.point: The only Nash equilibrium is now (Alder Late hours, Bexley Regular hours).

parts.sample: Bexley's Late payoffs fall to 15 and 40, so Regular hours is now better for Bexley whatever Alder does (20 > 15 and 45 > 40). Alder's best response to Bexley's Regular hours is Late hours (60 > 48). The only Nash equilibrium is Alder Late hours, Bexley Regular hours.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Using the original matrix, before the fee, identify the cell that gives the two stores the largest combined profit.

rubric.point: Both stores keep Regular hours (48 + 45 = 93), which is not the Nash equilibrium.

parts.sample: Adding the two payoffs in each cell gives 55, 80, 90 and 93. The largest is both stores keeping Regular hours: 48 + 45 = 93 (hundred dollars). It is not the Nash equilibrium: from there Bexley would switch to Late hours (55 > 45).
